self_assessment: Promoted tsh's private makeTableWithTruncatedColumn into the reusable asciitable.MakeTableWithTruncatedColumn(columnOrder, rows, truncatedColumn): it reads the terminal width via term.GetSize and falls back to 80 when that fails, gives every non-truncated column a maximum width of (width - 16) / (columns - 1), then hands the remaining space to the designated column so it expands and is truncated with an ellipsis. When the truncated column name matches no header, no column is expanded and all columns render at their computed widths with nothing dropped. tsh.go now keeps a one-line makeTableWithTruncatedColumn that delegates to the new exported function - I kept the private wrapper rather than deleting it so the package's existing test file still compiles - and its now-unused golang.org/x/term import was removed. api/types/app.go gained (a *AppV3) GetTeleportVersion() returning a.Version alongside the existing GetVersion. Verified: both modules build, gofmt clean, and a scratch copy of the repo's own three-case table test (truncating the middle column, the last column, and a non-matching name) passes against the new exported function with byte-identical output and the expected 80/80/93 row widths; ./lib/asciitable passes. Note: the environment's disk filled up during this task and I reclaimed it with go clean -cache -modcache, which does not affect the patch.
